title: Intervals & inequality notation
examples: When do we use square brackets versus parentheses?
What does the symbol infinity mean in this context?
How do I write an interval that goes from negative infinity to a number?

explain.say: Today we learn about writing sets using intervals. This notation is very useful for showing ranges of numbers.

items: Useful for representing sets of numbers

explain.say: A closed interval uses square brackets. This means the endpoints are included in the set. For example, the interval from two to five is written as two to five.
An open interval uses parentheses. This means the endpoints are not included in the set at all. For example, the interval from two to five is written as two to five.

We also use infinity in interval notation. Infinity always uses a parenthesis because you can never actually reach it. The interval from negative infinity to three is written as negative infinity to three.

faq.q: What is the difference between a parenthesis and a square bracket?
faq.a: A square bracket means the number is included in the set. A parenthesis means the number is not included in the set.
asks: When should I use square brackets?
Does a parenthesis mean less than or greater than?

faq.q: Can I use square brackets with infinity?
faq.a: No, you must always use a parenthesis when infinity is one of the endpoints. Infinity is not a number you can reach.
asks: Is infinity always with a parenthesis?
What symbol do I use for infinity?

faq.q: If I see negative infinity to x, what does that mean?
faq.a: It means all numbers less than or equal to x. If it is negative infinity to x, it means all numbers less than x.
asks: How do I show all numbers smaller than a value?
What does negative infinity mean in an interval?

faq.q: Does the order of the numbers matter?
faq.a: Yes, the smaller number must always come first in the interval notation. This keeps the notation correct.
asks: Do I write the smaller number first?
What if I write the bigger number first?

faq.q: What is the notation for all real numbers?
faq.a: All real numbers are represented by negative infinity to positive infinity. This is written as negative infinity to positive infinity.
asks: How do I write the entire number line?
What is the interval for all real numbers?

facts: Closed intervals use square brackets, like [a, b].
Open intervals use parentheses, like (a, b).
Infinity always requires a parenthesis, like (–∞, b].
The smaller number always comes first in the interval notation.

quiz.say: Which notation represents all numbers greater than or equal to minus three and less than ten?
quiz.why: The square bracket on minus three means it is included, and the parenthesis on ten means it is excluded.

wrong.1: This is wrong because it incorrectly excludes minus three, which should be included.
wrong.2: This is wrong because it incorrectly includes ten, which should be excluded.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it incorrectly includes ten, which should be excluded.

quiz.say: What is the correct interval notation for numbers greater than or equal to zero?
quiz.why: The square bracket shows zero is included, and the parenthesis is used correctly for infinity.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you cannot use a square bracket with infinity.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it is not standard interval notation.
wrong.3: This is wrong because it excludes zero, but the problem stated it was greater than or equal to zero.

quiz.say: If a set includes all real numbers, how is it written?
quiz.why: All real numbers means from negative infinity to positive infinity, using parentheses both times.

wrong.0: This is wrong because it lacks the necessary parentheses to show it is an interval.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it incorrectly includes infinity, which is impossible.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you cannot use a square bracket with infinity.
